points.title: 南方童年
points.description: 福克纳出生于密西西比州一个没落的南方贵族家庭，在这里度过了他的童年和青少年时期。他的曾祖父威廉·福克纳上校是南北战争中的英雄，这一家族历史深刻影响了福克纳的创作。在牛津镇，他接受了传统南方教育，但表现出对学校常规的抵触。这段时期，他开始接触文学，深受浪漫主义和维多利亚时期文学的影响，同时也观察到了南方社会的种族矛盾和旧秩序的衰落，这些主题后来成为他作品的核心。
points.descriptionEn: Faulkner was born into a declining Southern aristocratic family in Oxford, Mississippi, where he spent his childhood and adolescence. His great-grandfather, Colonel William Falkner, was a hero of the Civil War, and this family history profoundly influenced his writing. In Oxford, he received a traditional Southern education but showed resistance to conventional schooling. During this period, he began to engage with literature, deeply influenced by Romanticism and Victorian literature, while also observing the racial tensions and the decline of the old social order in the South, themes that later became central to his work.

points.title: 文学探索
points.description: 福克纳在密西西比大学短暂就读，但未完成学业。随后他前往纽约，在一家书店工作并开始尝试写作。这一时期，他出版了第一部诗集《大理石牧神》，并创作了第一部小说《士兵的报酬》。虽然这些早期作品并未获得成功，但福克纳已经开始形成自己独特的写作风格。他在纽约接触了现代主义文学，特别是乔伊斯和伍尔夫的作品，这对他的创作产生了深远影响。1925年，他返回南方，决心以南方为背景创作真正属于自己的文学世界。
points.descriptionEn: Faulkner briefly attended the University of Mississippi but did not complete his degree. He then moved to New York, where he worked in a bookstore and began to write. During this period, he published his first poetry collection, 'The Marble Faun,' and wrote his first novel, 'Soldiers' Pay.' Although these early works were not successful, Faulkner was beginning to develop his unique writing style. In New York, he was exposed to modernist literature, particularly the works of Joyce and Woolf, which profoundly influenced his writing. In 1925, he returned to the South, determined to create his own literary world set in the South.

points.title: 创作突破
points.description: 在新奥尔良，福克纳结识了作家舍伍德·安德森，后者成为他的导师和支持者。在安德森的鼓励下，福克纳开始创作他所谓的'约克纳帕塔法县'系列小说，以虚构的南方小镇为背景。这一时期，他创作了《萨托里斯》、《喧哗与骚动》和《我弥留之际》等重要作品。《喧哗与骚动》的出版标志着福克纳文学创作的重大突破，这部作品通过多视角叙事和意识流技巧，深刻描绘了南方康普生家族的衰落。尽管评论界开始关注他的作品，但福克纳的经济状况依然困难，他不得不回到牛津镇，在邮政局工作以维持生计。
points.descriptionEn: In New Orleans, Faulkner met writer Sherwood Anderson, who became his mentor and supporter. With Anderson's encouragement, Faulkner began what he called his 'Yoknapatawpha County' series of novels, set in a fictional Southern town. During this period, he wrote important works such as 'Sartoris,' 'The Sound and the Fury,' and 'As I Lay Dying.' The publication of 'The Sound and the Fury' marked a major breakthrough in Faulkner's literary career. Through multi-perspective narration and stream-of-consciousness techniques, the novel profoundly depicted the decline of the Southern Compson family. Although critics began to take notice of his work, Faulkner's financial situation remained difficult, forcing him to return to Oxford to work at the post office to make a living.

points.title: 文学巅峰
points.description: 这一时期是福克纳创作的高峰期，他在牛津镇创作了包括《八月之光》、《押沙龙，押沙龙！》、《熊》和《寓言》等代表作。福克纳构建了完整的'约克纳帕塔法县'文学世界，通过多部小说和短篇故事，描绘了南方社会的历史变迁和人性复杂性。他的作品采用了复杂的叙事结构、意识流技巧和南方哥特式风格，深刻探讨了种族、阶级、性别和道德等主题。尽管在美国国内获得有限认可，福克纳的作品在欧洲，特别是法国和英国，获得了高度评价，影响了存在主义文学的发展。1949年，他凭借《寓言》获得诺贝尔文学奖，成为美国文学史上最重要的作家之一。
points.descriptionEn: This period marked the peak of Faulkner's literary career. In Oxford, he wrote masterpieces including 'Light in August,' 'Absalom, Absalom!', 'The Bear,' and 'A Fable.' Faulkner constructed a complete literary world of 'Yoknapatawpha County,' through multiple novels and short stories, depicting the historical changes and human complexities of Southern society. His works employed complex narrative structures, stream-of-consciousness techniques, and Southern Gothic styles, deeply exploring themes of race, class, gender, and morality. Although receiving limited recognition in the United States, Faulkner's works were highly acclaimed in Europe, particularly in France and Britain, influencing the development of existentialist literature. In 1949, he won the Nobel Prize in Literature for 'A Fable,' becoming one of the most important figures in American literary history.

points.title: 晚年影响
points.description: 二战后，福克纳的声誉在美国国内逐渐提升，他的作品被广泛研究和教授。1950年代，他多次前往欧洲，包括担任巴黎美国文化中心的作家驻留项目。1957年至1962年，福克纳担任弗吉尼亚大学的创作学教授，在此期间他发表了著名的'福克纳在弗吉尼亚'演讲系列，分享他对文学和创作的见解。晚年，福克纳继续创作，但作品质量有所下降。1962年，他在密西西比州牛津镇因心脏病去世。福克纳去世后，他的文学地位进一步巩固，对世界文学产生了深远影响，特别是对拉美魔幻现实主义和南方文学传统的发展。
points.descriptionEn: After World War II, Faulkner's reputation in the United States gradually grew, and his works were widely studied and taught. In the 1950s, he made several trips to Europe, including participating in the writer-in-residence program at the American Cultural Center in Paris. From 1957 to 1962, Faulkner served as a professor of creative writing at the University of Virginia, during which time he delivered the famous 'Faulkner at Virginia' lecture series, sharing his insights on literature and writing. In his later years, Faulkner continued to write, but the quality of his work declined. In 1962, he died of a heart attack in Oxford, Mississippi. After his death, Faulkner's literary status was further consolidated, and he had a profound impact on world literature, particularly on the development of Latin American magical realism and the Southern literary tradition.

appraisal.zh: 福克纳被公认为美国南方文学传统的代表和20世纪最重要的英语作家之一，他以意识流与多重视角构建的“约克纳帕塔法县”系列革新了现代小说，深刻探讨了历史记忆与道德困境，并影响了后世众多作家。也有研究者指出，他的叙事晦涩难读，对南方旧秩序有所美化，对种族与女性问题的处理带有时代偏见，后期作品亦参差不齐。这些争议并未动摇其文学史地位。
appraisal.en: Faulkner is widely recognized as a representative of the Southern literary tradition and one of the most important English-language writers of the twentieth century. Through stream of consciousness and multiple perspectives, his Yoknapatawpha series transformed the modern novel, probing historical memory and moral dilemma and influencing later writers. Yet researchers also note his obscure style, a tendency to romanticize the old Southern order, treatments of race and women marked by the biases of his time, and uneven later work. Such disputes have not shaken his standing.

supporter.zh: 福克纳被赞誉为美国文学巨匠，其创新性的叙事技巧和深刻的南方主题探索开创了现代小说的新纪元。支持者认为他通过复杂的意识流叙事和多重视角，成功捕捉了人类心理的复杂性和南方社会的变迁。他的'约克纳帕塔法县'系列构建了完整的文学宇宙，对美国文学产生了革命性影响。福克纳的作品不仅展现了文学技巧的精湛，更深刻探讨了人类普遍的生存困境、道德选择和历史记忆，使他成为世界文学史上不可忽视的重要人物。
supporter.en: Faulkner is celebrated as a giant of American literature, whose innovative narrative techniques and profound exploration of Southern themes revolutionized the modern novel. Supporters argue that through complex stream-of-consciousness narration and multiple perspectives, he successfully captured the complexity of human psychology and the transformation of Southern society. His 'Yoknapatawpha County' series created a complete literary universe that had a revolutionary impact on American literature. Faulkner's works not only demonstrate exquisite literary craftsmanship but also deeply explore universal human dilemmas, moral choices, and historical memory, establishing him as an indispensable figure in world literary history.

critic.zh: 批评者指出福克纳的作品存在明显的局限性，包括对南方种族关系的复杂处理、男性中心主义视角以及晦涩难懂的叙事风格。一些评论家认为他过度美化南方旧秩序，对种族问题的处理存在矛盾。此外，福克纳后期作品质量参差不齐，部分作品被认为缺乏早期作品的深度和创新。他的叙事实验虽然创新，但也使作品难以被普通读者接受，限制了其影响力的广度。批评者还质疑福克纳对女性角色的刻画，认为其作品反映了当时社会的性别偏见。
critic.en: Critics point out several limitations in Faulkner's work, including his complex treatment of Southern racial relations, male-centered perspective, and often obscure narrative style. Some argue that he romanticized the old Southern order and held contradictory views on racial issues. Additionally, Faulkner's later works vary in quality, with some considered lacking the depth and innovation of his earlier pieces. While his narrative experiments were innovative, they also made his work difficult for general readers to access, limiting the breadth of his influence. Critics also question Faulkner's portrayal of female characters, suggesting his work reflects the gender biases of his time.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，福克纳被定义为美国南方文学传统的代表人物，其作品成为研究美国南方历史和文化的重要文本。他的文学技巧影响了包括加西亚·马尔克斯在内的众多作家，推动了现代主义和后现代主义文学的发展。福克纳的'约克纳帕塔法县'已成为文学地理学的经典案例，展示了作家如何通过虚构空间反映现实社会。在流行文化中，福克纳被视为文学天才的象征，其生平和作品被多次改编为电影和戏剧。尽管存在争议，福克纳被公认为20世纪最重要的英语作家之一，其文学遗产持续影响着当代文学创作和批评理论。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Faulkner is defined as a representative figure of the American Southern literary tradition, with his works serving as important texts for studying American Southern history and culture. His literary techniques have influenced numerous writers, including Gabriel García Márquez, and advanced the development of modernist and postmodernist literature. Faulkner's 'Yoknapatawpha County' has become a classic case study in literary geography, demonstrating how writers can use fictional spaces to reflect real societies. In popular culture, Faulkner is regarded as a symbol of literary genius, with his life and works adapted into films and dramas multiple times. Despite controversies, Faulkner is widely recognized as one of the most important English-language writers of the 20th century, whose literary legacy continues to influence contemporary literary creation and critical theory.

self.zh: 过去从未死亡，它甚至没有过去。
self.en: The past is never dead. It's not even past.
